section_summary: This section begins with 1941 diplomatic and naval intelligence concerning the Nanyo Kohatsu Kaisha’s links to the Japanese government and navy, fortification work in the Japanese-mandated Pacific islands, an alleged Japanese espionage case, tanker-fueling requests, and changes in Japanese shipping to the Netherlands East Indies. It then contains several copies of a February 1942 London despatch and its Times enclosure summarizing Dutch evidence of long-term Japanese economic penetration, espionage, propaganda, and fifth-column organization. The final pages transmit and begin the official pamphlet A Decade of Japanese Underground Activities in the Netherland East Indies, which places those activities within a broader account of Japanese expansionism and describes commercial, student, Islamic, and press-propaganda operations.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 5472: British Despatch Regarding Activities of the Japanese Nanyo Development Company
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Transmits a British report based on seized Nanyo Kohatsu Kaisha records linking the company to Japanese government ministries, the navy, and Pacific fortification work.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards a British consul-general's despatch concerning the activities and scope of the Nanyo Development Company. He states that company archives seized by the Netherlands East Indies government confirm close relations with the Japanese foreign and overseas-affairs ministries and the navy, as well as fortification work in the Japanese-mandated islands.

subfiles.title: British Consulate-General despatch no. 6 on the Nanyo Kohatsu Kaisha
subfiles.from: H. C. Walsh, British Consul-General, Batavia
subfiles.to: His Majesty's Principal Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs, London
subfiles.about: Reports evidence from seized company archives concerning Japanese military construction, naval cooperation, and southward-expansion plans.
subfiles.summary: Walsh: Dutch authorities seized Nanyo Kohatsu Kaisha's Manokwari archives; letters show military work contracts, Spratly surveys and Malakal harbor construction, linking leaders to expansion toward New Guinea, Timor and Celebes.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase concerning Lt. Col. Hashida and Japanese tanker requests
subfiles.about: Relays a report of Hashida's arrest for espionage and Japanese requests to refuel an unusually large number of tankers.
subfiles.summary: Lt. Col. Hashida, with detailed Australian industrial information, was arrested for espionage in the Dutch East Indies and deported; a request to fuel four tankers was refused and rescheduled.

subfiles.title: Duplicate paraphrase concerning Lt. Col. Hashida and Japanese tanker requests
subfiles.about: Duplicates the intelligence report on Hashida's deportation and Japanese tanker-fueling requests.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate paraphrase on Hashida's arrest and the refused and revised tanker fueling requests.

subfiles.title: CINCAF report on reduced Japanese shipping in Netherlands East Indies ports
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, United States Asiatic Fleet
subfiles.about: Reports a marked decline in Japanese vessels present or expected in Netherlands East Indies ports.
subfiles.summary: CINCAF: Japanese vessels in Netherlands East Indies ports and expected arrivals were markedly below previous levels, per the Batavia shipping adviser.

subfiles.title: Duplicate CINCAF report on reduced Japanese shipping
subfiles.from: Commander in Chief, United States Asiatic Fleet
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report of reduced Japanese ship movements in the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate CINCAF report that Japanese shipping in Netherlands East Indies ports was markedly lower.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on alleged political activities of Yoshisumi Tomegoro and Toyoshima Ataru
subfiles.about: Points to another file concerning a conversation between W. G. Lovink and Japanese Consul-General Ishizawa about two Japanese residents' alleged political activities.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: Lovink's talk with the Japanese consul-general about undesirable political activities of Yoshisumi Tomegoro and Toyoshima Ataru (702.94564/4).

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 36: Japanese Espionage and Penetration in the Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.from: A. J. Drexel Biddle Jr., American Embassy near the Netherlands Government, London
subfiles.about: Transmits a Times summary of a forthcoming Netherlands government report on Japanese espionage and penetration.
subfiles.summary: Biddle encloses a newspaper summary of the Dutch report and explains that publication of the full version is awaiting photographs. A Dutch official says additional valuable evidence will remain unpublished but may be obtainable by the American consul-general at Batavia from local authorities.

subfiles.title: The Times: Japanese Agents in Dutch Islands—A Sinister Economic Invasion Before Armed Attack
subfiles.about: Summarizes Dutch allegations that Japan used commercial enterprises, propaganda, consulates, and spies to prepare the Netherlands East Indies for conquest.
subfiles.summary: The Times: Japanese economic penetration through cheap goods, subsidized firms and forestry ventures; student recruitment, press schemes, propaganda, espionage, a puppet-regime plan for Java; the fifth column was largely interned.

subfiles.title: Duplicate despatch no. 36: Japanese Espionage and Penetration in the Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.from: A. J. Drexel Biddle Jr., American Embassy near the Netherlands Government, London
subfiles.about: Duplicates Biddle's transmittal of The Times summary and his note about unpublished Dutch intelligence.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats that the full Netherlands government report was delayed pending photographs and would also be published in the United States. It notes that omitted material remained in Netherlands East Indies files and might be supplied to the American consul-general at Batavia.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Times clipping: Japanese Agents in Dutch Islands
subfiles.about: Repeats the newspaper's synopsis of Dutch evidence concerning Japanese economic, political, and espionage preparations in the East Indies.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate Times clipping: subsidized firms as espionage bases, manipulation of students, politicians, press and religious opinion, the Kobayashi mission and wartime internment.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of despatch no. 36: Japanese Espionage and Penetration in the Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.from: A. J. Drexel Biddle Jr., American Embassy near the Netherlands Government, London
subfiles.about: Provides another copy of Biddle's despatch concerning the Dutch espionage report and potentially available unpublished evidence.
subfiles.summary: The despatch transmits the Times summary of the Netherlands government report and explains the delay in publishing the full document. It again suggests that American representatives at Batavia might obtain confidential evidence excluded from the published version.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 38: Pamphlet on Japanese Underground Activities in the Netherlands East Indies
subfiles.from: A. J. Drexel Biddle Jr., American Embassy near the Netherlands Government, London
subfiles.about: Transmits five copies of the now-published full Netherlands government report on Japanese underground activity.
subfiles.summary: Referring to despatch no. 36 and its Times summary, Biddle reports that the complete study has now appeared. He forwards five copies under the title A Decade of Japanese Underground Activities in the Netherlands East Indies.

subfiles.title: Department of State transmittal of despatch no. 38 and its enclosure
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division; Office of Naval Intelligence; Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Distributes the London embassy's despatch and enclosed pamphlet to United States military, naval, and federal investigative agencies.
subfiles.summary: State sends confidential Despatch No. 38 on Japanese underground activities in the Netherlands East Indies to intelligence offices.

subfiles.title: A Decade of Japanese Underground Activities in the Netherland East Indies
subfiles.about: Presents the Dutch government's case that Japan spent decades preparing political, economic, and military penetration of the Netherlands East Indies.
subfiles.summary: The pamphlet's preface justifies the Netherlands declaration of war after the December 1941 attacks and argues that Japanese designs on the South Seas had been systematically prepared for at least twenty-five years. It contrasts Dutch colonial administration and its open-door policy with Japanese rule in Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria, and occupied China, then surveys Japan's territorial expansion and repeated denials of aggressive intent. The section describes early reconnaissance by fishermen and photographers, the commercial drive of 1931–1932, Nanshin-ron and Pan-Asian organizations, attempts to recruit Indonesian students and Muslims, and Japanese efforts to influence Malay-, Chinese-, Japanese-, and Dutch-language newspapers. The pamphlet continues beyond page 39.
